problem:
Given that $f(x)=|x-1|-2,$ on which of the following intervals is $f(x)$ invertible?

- $x\in (-\infty ,1]$
- $x\in (1,\infty )$
- $x\in (-\infty ,2]$

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14068486/assets/1eccd6630b69558f8a86f8336e9f0e49f37ffb29acf4a3c8f58be34346b4c93c.png)

On which of the following intervals is the function $f(x)$ (shown above) invertible?

- $x\in [-2,0]$
- $x\in (-3,-2]$
- $x\in (-3,-1]$
feedback.worked_solution:
A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test. 

- The given function is **not** invertible on each of the intervals $x\in [-2,0]$  and $x\in (-3,-1]$ because some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14068486/assets/d8cc826df6fed7a4106539d88ffa8a1fdc0529904497c2d5413f9761acaccd12.png)

        

- The given function is invertible on the interval $x\in (-3,-2].$ Indeed, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14068486/assets/bc00ed8f4bdf03b248dbd9a1651ed073e352d512b830139505fba3b60e05e7e9.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is " II only".
